mainTopic: Where the borders of ארץ ישראל run: ships, flowerpots, the sea and its islands, עכו, and the mixed status of סוריא
overview: The amud opens by finishing a doubt about a flowerpot with a hole in it, resting off the ground. Does it count like the land, the way a ship's soil might? One way to look at it: a ship is weaker because it moves around, while a pot stays put. The other way: a ship is stronger because water is like solid ground, while a pot has air underneath it. רב נחמן בר יצחק then says the ship dispute applies only on the ים הגדול, since everyone agrees about the rivers of ארץ ישראל. A ברייתא maps the borders using an imaginary string from טורי אמנון to נחל מצרים, and רבי יהודה adds that the sea opposite the land is also ארץ ישראל, based on the word ״וּגְבוּל״. The גמרא then turns to רבי מאיר's ruling about עכו and proves from it that selling a slave to סוריא is like selling him to חוצה לארץ. Finally, a ברייתא lists three ways סוריא is like חוצה לארץ and three ways it is like ארץ ישראל. That list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A boat moves around, but a flowerpot stays put
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of one side of the doubt. רבי יהודה's ruling, that soil on a ship does not count as the land unless the ship touches bottom, may apply only because a ship moves around. It would not apply to a pot that stays in one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe רבי יהודה said a ship's soil does not count as the land only for a ship, which is built to move away. But a flowerpot is not built to move away, so for a pot even he might agree its soil counts as the land.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining in the middle of a sentence. The גמרא is laying out one possible side of a doubt about a flowerpot resting off the ground: a ship may be different because it is made to move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that soil on a ship does not count as part of the land unless the ship touches the bottom. This step suggests a reason: a ship is always on the move, so its soil is not really attached to any place. A flowerpot normally stays in one spot, so even when it rests off the ground, its soil might still count as attached.

keyTerms.meaning: A flowerpot (here, one with a hole in the bottom)
Made to move away; built to travel and not stay in one spot
A ship or boat

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a final ruling. It is only one side of a doubt, and the very next step offers the opposite way of looking at it.

phrases.english: which is made to move away,
phrases.notes: This picks up mid-sentence. The "which" is the ship from the line just before.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עָצִיץ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי לִבְרוֹחַ – לֹא.
phrases.english: but a flowerpot, which is not made to move away – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעֲשׂוּיָה לִבְרוֹחַ, אֲבָל עָצִיץ, שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָשׂוּי לִבְרוֹחַ – לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a sentence that began on the earlier part of the daf. It gives one side of the doubt about the flowerpot.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should a flowerpot with a hole, resting off the ground, be treated like a ship or not?

steps.title: Water counts like solid ground, but air does not
steps.stepSummary: The opposite side of the doubt. The רבנן may say a ship counts as the land only because water connects it to the ground. A flowerpot has air underneath it, which breaks that connection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe it works the other way. The רבנן said a ship counts as the land only because no air separates it from the ground, since water is treated like solid earth. But a flowerpot has air separating it from the ground, so it would not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now offers a second, opposite way of looking at the flowerpot. It uses the view of the רבנן, who treat the soil on a ship as part of the land even when the ship does not touch bottom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this approach, what matters is a physical connection, not whether the object moves. Water under a ship works like solid ground, so the ship's soil stays connected to the land. A pot resting on pegs has a gap of air below it, and that gap cuts it off. So here the ship counts and the pot does not, which is the reverse of Step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Alternatively; or you could say
The Sages (the majority view)
Air separates; there is a gap of air in between
Solid, firm ground

steps.whatToRemember: There are two opposite ways to compare a pot to a ship. Either moving is what matters (the ship is weaker), or a gap of air is what matters (the pot is weaker).

phrases.english: Alternatively:
the Rabbis only said
there, regarding a ship,
where no air separates it from the ground –
because water is like solid ground;
but a flowerpot, where air separates it – no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן הָתָם אֶלָּא בִּסְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse comparison to Step 1. Here the ship is stronger than the pot.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the key factor moving around (Step 1) or a gap of air (this step)?

steps.title: The ship dispute is only about the Mediterranean
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that on the rivers inside ארץ ישראל everyone agrees a ship counts as ארץ ישראל. The argument is only about a ship in the ים הגדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: on the rivers of ארץ ישראל, everyone agrees. When they argue, it is about the Great Sea.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק narrows down where the earlier argument about a ship really applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not explain the dispute by how a ship relates to the ground. He explains it by location. A river inside ארץ ישראל is surely part of the land, so nobody argues there. The open question is the Mediterranean, because it is unclear whether that sea counts as part of ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rivers
Everyone agrees; no one argues
The Great Sea, meaning the Mediterranean

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes what the dispute is about. The question is no longer about how a ship connects to the ground. It becomes a question of where the borders of ארץ ישראל run.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
regarding the rivers of the Land of Israel,
everyone agrees.
phrases.notes: They agree that a ship on such a river counts as being in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Rather, where they disagree is on the Great Sea.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: בִּנְהָרוֹת דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the flowerpot doubt behind and offers a new way to read the ship dispute, based on location.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ship on the rivers of ארץ ישראל counts as ארץ ישראל according to everyone. The dispute is only about a ship on the Mediterranean.

steps.title: A ברייתא maps the borders, including islands in the sea
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines ארץ ישראל on land from טורי אמנון inward. For islands in the sea, it pictures a string stretched from טורי אמנון to נחל מצרים. What is inside the line is ארץ ישראל, and what is outside is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: What is the Land and what is outside the Land? Everything sloping down from טורי אמנון inward is ארץ ישראל. From טורי אמנון outward is outside the Land. As for the islands in the sea, we picture a string stretched over them from טורי אמנון to נחל מצרים. From the string inward is ארץ ישראל. From the string outward is outside the Land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show why the Mediterranean is a real question. Part of the sea area can count as ארץ ישראל, and part cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On land, the border runs from the טורי אמנון mountains inward. Out at sea, an imaginary straight line from טורי אמנון in the north to נחל מצרים in the south decides which islands are in. Since the sea itself is split by this line, it makes sense to argue about a ship sailing on the Mediterranean.

keyTerms.meaning: Outside the Land of Israel
The Amnon mountains, a northern border point
Islands
A string pulled tight; an imaginary straight line
The Brook of Egypt, the southern border point

steps.whatToRemember: An imaginary line from טורי אמנון to נחל מצרים divides the sea area. Inside the line counts as ארץ ישראל, and outside does not. That is why a ship on the Mediterranean is a real question.
steps.confusionAlert: "Inward" (לפנים) means toward ארץ ישראל, and "outward" (לחוץ) means away from it. These words do not refer to the inside of an island.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
What is the Land, and what is outside the Land?
Everything that slopes and descends
from the Amnon mountains inward is the Land of Israel;
from the Amnon mountains outward is outside the Land.
As for the islands in the sea –

phrases.aramaic: רוֹאִין אוֹתָן כְּאִילּוּ חוּט מָתוּחַ עֲלֵיהֶם
phrases.english: we view them as if a string were stretched over them
from the Amnon mountains to the Brook of Egypt;
from the string inward is the Land of Israel;
from the string outward is outside the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵיזֶהוּ אֶרֶץ וְאֵיזֶהוּ חוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן בר יצחק by showing that part of the sea area can count as ארץ ישראל, so the Mediterranean is open to dispute.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the ship dispute is specifically about the ים הגדול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that defines the borders of ארץ ישראל, including the imaginary string from טורי אמנון to נחל מצרים for islands in the sea.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: everything opposite the Land counts as the Land
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says that any place in the sea that is lined up opposite ארץ ישראל is treated as ארץ ישראל, and he brings a פסוק about the western border.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: anything opposite ארץ ישראל is like ארץ ישראל, because the פסוק says, "And as the western border, you shall have the Great Sea and border; this shall be your western border."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step continues with a second opinion. רבי יהודה pushes the border of ארץ ישראל out into the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא only counted islands inside the line, not the sea itself. רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as saying the ים הגדול itself is part of the border. So for him, all the water lined up with the land is ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Opposite, lined up with
The western border (literally, the sea border)
The Great Sea, the Mediterranean

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument helps explain the earlier dispute about a ship in the ים הגדול. If the sea itself is ארץ ישראל, a ship sailing there is in the Land.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Anything that is opposite Eretz Yisrael
is like Eretz Yisrael,
as it is said:
"And as the western border,
you shall have the Great Sea and its border;
this shall be your western border."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁכְּנֶגֶד אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion within the same ברייתא quoted in step 4, disagreeing with the first opinion about the sea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the sea area lined up opposite ארץ ישראל has the status of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The string rule for islands off to the sides
steps.stepSummary: Islands that are not directly opposite the land are judged by imagined strings stretched west to the ocean from קפלוריא in the north and from נחל מצרים in the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: For islands off to the sides, picture a string stretched over them from קפלוריא to the Ocean, and from נחל מצרים to the Ocean. Inside the string is ארץ ישראל, and outside the string is חוצה לארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה's statement continues. He explains how to judge islands that sit a bit north or south of the strip directly opposite the land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two imagined lines run straight west, one from the northern point and one from the southern point. Anything between the two lines is ארץ ישראל. Anything beyond them is outside the Land.

keyTerms.meaning: Islands
A string pulled tight
The Ocean (the Atlantic), at the far western edge
Outside ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: And the islands that are off to the sides,
phrases.notes: He means islands a little north or south of the area directly opposite the land.

phrases.english: we view them as if
a string were stretched over them
from Kefalorya to the Ocean,
and from the River of Egypt to the Ocean;
from the string inward is Eretz Yisrael,
from the string outward is outside the Land.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the string in step 4. There, the first opinion ran one line along the coast from טורי אמנון to נחל מצרים. Here רבי יהודה runs two lines out west to the ocean.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַנִּסִּין שֶׁבַּצְּדָדִין, רוֹאִין אוֹתָן כְּאִילּוּ חוּט מָתוּחַ עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהודה's statement by defining the side edges of his sea border.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Islands between the two westward lines count as ארץ ישראל; islands beyond them are חוצה לארץ.

steps.title: How do the רבנן use the word ״וּגְבוּל״?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from ״וּגְבוּל״, since רבי יהודה used it to include the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this word ״וּגְבוּל״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the רבנן about the פסוק that רבי יהודה used. It wants to know what that word teaches according to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word ״וּגְבוּל״ seems to support רבי יהודה's idea that the sea is part of the border. The רבנן do not include the sea, so they must read the word some other way. The גמרא asks what that reading is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the majority opinion
What do they do with it, meaning how do they use this word

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: This is the first opinion in the ברייתא from step 4, which counted only the islands and not the sea.

phrases.english: this word "and border"
what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the other side of the ברייתא handles the פסוק that רבי יהודה brought in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from ״וּגְבוּל״ if not that the sea is part of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The word teaches about islands; רבי יהודה says islands need no verse
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use ״וּגְבוּל״ to include the islands. רבי יהודה holds that the islands are obvious and need no פסוק, so the word is free to teach about the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for the islands. And רבי יהודה? Islands don't need a verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use the word to teach that the islands are part of ארץ ישראל. It then explains why רבי יהודה does not read it that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the word teaches something. For the רבנן, it is needed to include the islands. רבי יהודה thinks the islands are clearly part of the Land without any פסוק, so he uses the word to include the sea itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it, meaning the פסוק is needed to teach something else
They don't need a פסוק, because it is obvious

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: the islands inside the line are ארץ ישראל, but the sea is not. רבי יהודה: the sea opposite the land is ארץ ישראל too, and the islands are obvious.

phrases.english: They need it for the islands.
And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: why doesn't he use the word for islands too?

phrases.english: Islands don't need a verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְנִסִּין. וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, נִסִּין לָא צְרִיכִי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 and explains why רבי יהודה reads the word differently.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use ״וּגְבוּל״ to include the islands. רבי יהודה says the islands need no פסוק, so the word teaches that the sea is included.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי מאיר on עכו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's statement that רבי מאיר considers עכו like ארץ ישראל, opening a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: עכו is like ארץ ישראל, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote the next line of the משנה. This sets up a new topic about places near the border.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of the sea border is finished. Now the גמרא turns to רבי מאיר's view in the משנה that עכו counts as ארץ ישראל for bringing a גט. This leads into the next question about another border area.

keyTerms.meaning: Akko, a city on the northern coast
Etc., meaning the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Akko is like Eretz Yisrael, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: עַכּוֹ – כְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New section: the גמרא leaves the sea-border discussion and quotes the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, עכו is treated like ארץ ישראל for the laws of bringing a גט.

steps.title: Is selling a slave to סוריא like selling him to חוצה לארץ?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רבי חייא בר אבא whether a man who sells his slave to סוריא is treated like one who sells him to חוצה לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי חייא בר אבא: one who sells his slave to סוריא, is he like one who sells to חוצה לארץ, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about סוריא, another border area. The גמרא is setting up a discussion of its status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who sells his slave to חוצה לארץ is penalized: the slave goes free. The question is whether סוריא counts as outside the Land for this rule, or is treated like ארץ ישראל. The answer comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him, a real question whose answer is not known
One who sells his slave
Syria, an area just outside the main borders of ארץ ישראל
Is he like, is it the same as

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: They asked Rabbi Chiya bar Abba:
One who sells his slave to Syria,
is he like one who sells outside the Land,
phrases.notes: Selling a slave outside the Land has a penalty: the slave goes free.

phrases.english: or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: הַמּוֹכֵר עַבְדּוֹ לְסוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After quoting רבי מאיר about עכו, the גמרא raises a related question about the status of סוריא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether סוריא counts as חוצה לארץ for the penalty on a man who sells his slave there.

steps.title: Answer from the משנה: סוריא counts as חוצה לארץ for slaves
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא proves from רבי מאיר's words in the משנה that selling a slave to סוריא is like selling him to חוצה לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You already learned this in the משנה. רבי מאיר says עכו is like ארץ ישראל for גיטין. That means for גיטין, yes, but for slaves, no. So סוריא, which is much farther away, is surely not like ארץ ישראל for slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers the רבנן's question from step 10 by pointing to the משנה they already know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר limited עכו's status as ארץ ישראל to גיטין, so we learn that for slaves עכו counts as outside the land. סוריא is farther from the heart of ארץ ישראל than עכו, so it cannot be treated better. This is a קל וחומר: selling a slave to סוריא is like selling him to חוצה לארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: You learned it (it is already in a source you know)
Akko, a city on the northern edge of ארץ ישראל
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
Which is much farther away

steps.whatToRemember: For selling slaves, סוריא counts as חוצה לארץ. If even עכו is not treated as ארץ ישראל for slaves, then surely סוריא is not.

phrases.english: He said to them: You have already learned it:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי חייא בר אבא, who was asked the question in step 10.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Akko is like Eretz Yisrael for bills of divorce;
for bills of divorce, yes; for slaves, no,
phrases.notes: This is what we learn from רבי מאיר mentioning only גיטין.

phrases.english: and all the more so Syria, which is much farther away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Selling a slave to סוריא is like selling him to חוצה לארץ, learned by קל וחומר from עכו in the משנה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: סוריא is like ארץ ישראל in three ways and like חוצה לארץ in three ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying סוריא has a mixed status: three ways like ארץ ישראל and three ways like חוצה לארץ, with a memory sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: In three ways סוריא is the same as ארץ ישראל, and in three ways it is the same as חוצה לארץ. (Memory sign: עב בר רק.)
steps.whatsHappening: Since סוריא just came up, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about its status. This line is the heading; the next steps list the details.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סוריא is not simply one or the other. It has a middle status, so we have to know case by case which rules treat it like ארץ ישראל and which treat it like חוצה לארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Syria, the lands conquered by דוד המלך north of ארץ ישראל
Outside of ארץ ישראל
A memory sign to help remember a list

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּרָכִים שָׁוְותָה סוּרְיָא לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: In three ways Syria is equal to Eretz Yisrael,
and in three ways to outside of the land.
(Mnemonic: Ayin-beit, beit-reish, reish-kuf.)
phrases.notes: These letters are just a memory aid hinting at the cases in the list. They aren't words to translate.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּרָכִים שָׁוְותָה סוּרְיָא לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of סוריא in step 11 by bringing a related ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סוריא has a mixed status: three rules like ארץ ישראל and three like חוצה לארץ.

steps.title: Three ways סוריא is like חוצה לארץ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the three ways סוריא is treated like חוצה לארץ: its earth is impure, selling a slave there, and bringing a גט from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Its earth is impure like חוצה לארץ. Someone who sells his slave to סוריא is like someone who sells him to חוצה לארץ. And someone who brings a גט from סוריא is like someone who brings one from חוצה לארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now spells out the three ways סוריא counts as חוצה לארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slave rule matches exactly what רבי חייא בר אבא proved in step 11. The גט rule means a שליח bringing a גט from סוריא must say בפני נכתב ובפני נחתם, just like one bringing it from חוצה לארץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Its earth is ritually impure
One who sells his slave
One who brings a bill of divorce (a שליח)

steps.confusionAlert: The heading in step 12 mentioned ארץ ישראל first, but the list starts with the חוצה לארץ cases. Don't get mixed up: these three are the 'outside the land' rules.

phrases.english: Its soil is impure, like outside of the land,
and one who sells his slave to Syria
is like one who sells him outside of the land.
And one who brings a bill of divorce from Syria
is like one who brings it from outside of the land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the list announced in step 12.
steps.whyThisMatters: The ברייתא openly confirms the answer to the question from step 10 about selling a slave to סוריא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For impurity of its earth, selling slaves, and bringing a גט, סוריא is treated like חוצה לארץ.

steps.title: Three ways סוריא is like ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins listing the three ways סוריא is like ארץ ישראל: מעשר and שביעית, entering it in purity, and buying a field there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in three ways it is like ארץ ישראל: its produce must have מעשר taken and follows the rules of שביעית like ארץ ישראל; someone who wants to enter it while staying pure may enter; and someone who buys a field in סוריא...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now lists the ways סוריא counts as ארץ ישראל. The third case, buying a field, starts here, and its ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the מצוות tied to the land, מעשר and שביעית, סוריא is treated like ארץ ישראל. Even though its earth is impure (step 13), a person who wants to stay pure is still allowed to go in. The ruling on the field continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithes taken from produce
The seventh year, when the land rests
In a state of ritual purity
One who buys a field

phrases.english: And in three ways it is like Eretz Yisrael:
it is obligated in tithe and in the Sabbatical Year, like Eretz Yisrael,
and one who wishes to enter it in purity may enter,
and one who buys a field in Syria —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the 'outside the land' rules to the 'like the land' rules announced in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For מעשר, שביעית, and entering in purity, סוריא is treated like ארץ ישראל. The third rule, about buying a field, continues on the next amud.
